AdditionalPermissions.description:
Extra room asked for by one command.

Only ever widens: a caller cannot use it to narrow the session's policy, because narrowing by
request would let one command quietly change what a later command is allowed to assume.

network_access.description: Whether this command may reach the network.

writable_roots.description: Roots outside the workspace this command may write.

Attempt.description: One attempt, recorded whether or not it produced anything.

degraded.description: Fields this attempt could not honour.

model.description: The target. Empty for a preflight refusal, which never had one.

oneOf.description:
It did not. Present even when a partial answer was streamed, because that one still
cost money.

AttemptPhase.description: Where in a call an attempt happened.

oneOf.description: Compiling and checking, before anything was sent.
The first attempt for the chosen target.
Another try at the same target.
A hop to the next target.

ConfigPatch.description:
A partial update to a session's mutable configuration.

The wiring — kind, sandbox, workspace — is not here, because it is decided when the session
opens and is not the application's to change while it runs. Everything in this struct is
content or strategy, and every field is optional: absent means unchanged, `null` (where the
field is doubly optional) means cleared.

hints.description: Adapter hints. Merged field by field.

params.description: Generation parameters. Replaces the whole block, because every field is already optional.

routing.description: The route this session takes. Absent means unchanged.

tools.description: The tool allow-list. Empty means every registered tool.

changed.description: The fields that actually changed, in the order they were applied.

DataPart.description:
Structured output. JSON text rather than bytes, because JSON is UTF-8 by definition and
text is what every toolchain can read.

Degraded.description:
A field the provider could not honour.

Recorded rather than swallowed: a `tool_choice = Required` that quietly became `Auto` is a
session behaving differently than it was configured to, and the difference is
undiscoverable afterwards.

DescribeResponse.description: What a caller learns before it starts anything.

abi_version.description: The ABI version it speaks, from the schema's own `$id`.

models.description: The models a route may name.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of a failed request.

One shape for every failure: a caller should not have to know which endpoint it called to
know how to read why it failed.

code.description: A stable category programs match on.

retry_after_millis.description: When to retry, in milliseconds. Absent means no hint.

retryable.description: A statement about this request, not about the world.

ErrorCode.description:
A stable error category.

Codes are enums rather than strings because the first caller who compares a string
freezes it forever.

oneOf.description: The thing named does not exist.

Event.description:
An append-only record of something that happened.

`seq` is dense and gap-free, which is what makes it usable as a resume cursor without
a separate acknowledgement protocol. `schema_version` is written alongside the event so
a reader can upcast instead of guessing.

at_unix_millis.description: Unix milliseconds, from the injected clock so replay is deterministic.

schema_version.description: The schema this event was written with.

seq.description: Monotonic within a session, starting at 0.

EventKind.description:
The payload of an [`Event`].

Events carry the content model rather than copies of its fields — [`ToolCall`] here is
the same type a [`ToolCallPart`] holds — so a live stream and a stored history cannot
disagree about the shape of an answer.

oneOf.description: A session state transition, with the reason when it is terminal.

stop.description: Set when the state is terminal.

part_index.description:
Which part of the message it belongs to.

Without it a client cannot tell a second text block from a continuation of the
first, so text → tool call → more text is unrepresentable in the stream.

oneOf.description:
A fragment of a reasoning trace.

`signature` usually arrives on its own, in a delta with empty `text`: a provider
signs the finished block rather than each fragment.

part_index.description: Which part of the message it belongs to.

signature.description: The provider's signature fragment, returned verbatim.

oneOf.description: A tool call began. Its arguments follow as [`EventKind::ToolCallArgs`].

index.description: Position in this turn's tool-call list.

progress_token.description: When set, the tool reports progress under this token.

tool_call_id.description: The correlation id the result will be filed under.

oneOf.description:
A fragment of one call's arguments.

Arguments stream as text because that is what providers send and because a partial
object cannot be handed to a tool. The kernel assembles and validates before anything
runs; malformed arguments become a result the model can read.

index.description: Which call this fragment belongs to.

result.description: The result — the same value that enters history.

usage.description:
What the tool reported it spent, when it reported anything.

Absent is not zero: a tool that says nothing has not said it was free.

oneOf.description: One model call's consumption, debited whether or not the answer was usable.

attempt_index.description: Which attempt in the ledger it belongs to.

model.description: The model that served it, after routing.

purpose.description: Why the call happened, so a summary's spend can be told from an answer's.

oneOf.description:
The session's mutable configuration changed.

Recorded because a replay has to know which system prompt was in force at turn 42; without
it, the log would rebuild a conversation that never happened.

A field the provider could not honour.

Reported, never swallowed: a `tool_choice = Required` that quietly became `Auto` is a
session behaving differently than it was configured to.

One attempt ended badly. Recorded because a retry does not erase the attempt that failed,
or the money it spent.
A policy verdict of `AskHuman` was reached.

default_if_unanswered.description: What the kernel does if nobody answers. A refusal, not a silent approval.

options.description:
Typed answers, so a client can render "once" and "always" differently and the
verdict can say which was chosen.

oneOf.description:
The session moved to a newer tool-source generation.

Recorded rather than inferred, so a replay reproduces which tool set each turn ran
against.

The assembled message a model call produced.

Deltas are a rendering protocol; this is the record. Some content can only be
assembled — a reasoning signature arrives as its own delta — and a client that joins
late should render without replaying every fragment.

message.description: The message, as it enters history.

step_index.description: Which step of the turn produced it.

argv.description: What was run, verbatim, so an audit can see it.

pid.description: The process id, when the platform gave one.

policy.description: The policy it ran under, after any granted widening.

oneOf.description: A chunk of a command's output.

Bytes written to a running process's stdin.

Recorded because it is the most audit-worthy thing in the system: spawning `/bin/sh` is
safe, writing `rm -rf /` into it is not.

Progress from a long-running call. A call whose only feedback is a deadline is
indistinguishable from a hang.

total.description: Units expected. Zero means unknown, not zero.

exit_code.description: The exit status, or `-1` when the process was killed by a signal.

timed_out.description: Whether it was killed for exceeding its deadline.

ExecRequest.description: One command to run inside the session's sandbox.

argv.description: The command line. No shell by default: an argv cannot be word-split by accident.

cwd.description: Where to run it. Absent means the session's workspace.

permissions.description: What to ask for on top of the session's policy.

timeout_millis.description: Wall-clock ceiling. Absent means the session's remaining budget.

ExecStream.description: Which stream a chunk came from.

FilePart.description:
A reference to content that is not carried here: an artifact, a workspace file, or a
truncated tool result's spill.

This is also how truncation is expressed. A result too large to store is spilled; the
text keeps a marker and this part keeps the pointer. That is a policy outcome, not an
error.

GenerateParams.description:
What the caller wants from one call.

Every field is carried, not decided: the kernel has no opinion about sampling. They live
here rather than as a bag of extras because a bag is a second extension hatch, and these are
the parameters every provider has.

format.description: The shape the answer must have.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Whether one turn may call several tools at once.

In the contract rather than in an adapter because the *kernel* acts on it: `invoke_tools`
fans a batch out concurrently. A provider that forbids it and a kernel that does it anyway
would disagree about what happened in a turn.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort, for models that expose one.

stop.description:
Sequences that end the completion.

Not every provider has this — the OpenAI Responses API rejects it outright — so an adapter
that cannot send it reports a [`Degraded`] rather than dropping it in silence.

Generation.description:
A tool-source generation.

Generations are immutable snapshots of the declared sources. A session is pinned to
one at start and may only move forward at a turn boundary, and only when the two
generations are compatible.

Hints.description:
Preferences an adapter may honour, and must report when it cannot.

Separate from [`GenerateParams`] because these change while a session runs — a conversation
that is filling its window wants less prose, and a review turn wants more detail — and because
they are *hints*: an adapter that has no channel for one reports a [`Degraded`] rather than
failing the call.

max_tool_calls.description: A ceiling on tool calls in one response.

metadata.description: Labels the provider echoes back, up to sixteen.

reasoning_summary.description: How much of the reasoning to summarise.

service_tier.description: The cost/latency trade this session prefers.

truncation.description: What to do when the conversation does not fit.

verbosity.description: How much prose an answer should carry.

InferenceRequest.description:
One inference: the messages to send.

The messages are the caller's, not the session's. What you send is what you get, and whether
the answer enters history is the next request's business — which is what makes a verification
turn possible without polluting the transcript.

messages.description: The conversation to send, oldest first. Absent sends nothing.

finish.description: The provider's own reason for stopping.

message.description: The assistant message. Nothing has been appended to the session.

usage.description: What the session has spent so far.

Ledger.description: Every attempt a call made, and the sum.

total.description: The sum across every attempt that produced tokens.

MediaSource.description:
Bytes, or a reference to them, plus the type that makes them renderable.

`url` exists because inlining a large image into an event log is a storage incident: the
log is append-only and replayed, so every byte is paid for on every replay. `data` exists
because a caller with no reachable store must still be able to send one.

media_type.description: The media type, e.g. `image/png`. Required: bytes without a type are not renderable.

content.description:
What it contains.

Non-empty whenever the kernel writes one: an empty content is a bug in whatever
produced it, not something a reader has to tolerate.

OutputChunk.description:
A piece of captured output, and whether it was cut.

Truncation is carried rather than applied silently: a model that cannot see that its output
was shortened will reason about a file it only half read.

truncated_after_lines.description: The line after which the rest was dropped, when it was.

Part.description:
One piece of content.

The union is small on purpose: seven kinds. Audio and video are [`PartKind::File`] with an
`audio/*` or `video/*` media type, because the kernel moves those bytes and never
interprets them. A kind is added when the kernel must act differently — not when a
provider can emit something new.

oneOf.description: A reference to content that is not carried here.
The model asking for a tool.
A tool's answer, folded back into history.

meta.description:
Contextual or vendor-specific data.

The kernel never reads it, never interprets it, and never rejects an unknown key.
This is the only extension hatch: a schema with two of them has everyone using the
other one.

PendingCall.description:
A call waiting on a human.

Part of the snapshot because the wait outlives any process: a session parked on a
confirmation must be resumable tomorrow, and the call it is holding has to come back with
it.

call.description: The call that has not run.

PermissionKind.description: The kinds of answer a permission request offers.

oneOf.description: Allow this call and, if the host agrees, this tool for the session.

PermissionOption.description:
What a human may answer when a call is gated.

The kernel *reports* the choice; it never decides that "always" applies. That is policy,
and it belongs to the host.

id.description: Caller-chosen, returned verbatim in the verdict.

ProcessInfo.description: One running process, as a listing sees it.

process.description: The command, and where it is.

ProcessListResponse.description: The processes this node is running.

ProcessSpec.description: How to start a process session.

argv.description: The command line. No shell by default: an argv cannot be word-split by accident.

cwd.description: Where to run it. Absent means the session's workspace.

permissions.description: What this command asks for on top of the session's policy.

ProcessStartRequest.description: A command to start as a process session.

argv.description: The command line. No shell by default: an argv cannot be word-split by accident.

cwd.description: Where to run it. Absent means the workspace below.

permissions.description: What to ask for on top of the session's policy.

sandbox.description: What its commands may touch. Set here because a process session is created by this call.

ProcessStartResponse.description: What starting a process answered with.

next_seq.description: The cursor a client reads its output from.

pid.description: The pid, when the platform gave one.

oneOf.description: No pid yet: the session exists, the process does not.
Running, under whatever isolation the platform could give.

The process is gone and we do not know how it ended.

A live process cannot be reconstructed from a log — its memory, its file descriptors and
its cursor are not in the event stream. So a session that outlives the runtime says this,
rather than pretending the command is still running.

Purpose.description:
Why a model call is happening.

The kernel makes calls of its own — a compaction summary is one — so the purpose has to be
first-class: a budget whose summarisation spend is indistinguishable from answer spend is a
budget nobody can explain after the fact.

oneOf.description: The answer the caller is waiting for.
Another try at a turn that produced something unusable.

ReasoningEffort.description: How hard a reasoning model should think.

ReasoningPart.description:
One provider reasoning trace.

`signature` is why this is not a plain string: some providers sign a reasoning block and
reject the next turn when the signature is not returned verbatim. Dropping it turns a
multi-turn session into a failure on turn two. `id` and `source` exist for the same
reason — they are opaque to the kernel and must round-trip.

id.description: The provider's item id, when it uses one.

text.description: The reasoning text. May be empty when the provider withholds it.

Role.description:
Who produced a message.

The set is the smallest one every provider can express. A provider with a fifth role
maps it onto one of these in its adapter — the kernel does not learn it.

Routing.description:
The route a call takes, in order.

A chain rather than a name because the kernel owns retries and fallback: a runtime that
gives up on the first 503 has the availability of its least reliable provider.

chain.description: Candidate models, first that answers wins.

retries.description: Extra attempts against the same target before moving to the next.

oneOf.description: Run outside the sandbox. The gate turns this into a human question, not a formality.
Stay in the sandbox, with more room for this command only.

additional.description: What to add. Never what to remove.

SandboxPolicy.description:
What a session's commands may touch.

Set when the session opens and carried in its checkpoint. It is **not** a field of a request:
a caller that can name its own policy can name `DangerFullAccess`, and a permission slip the
untrusted side writes is not a permission model.

oneOf.description: No restriction. Use with caution, and only where the code is yours.
Write inside the session's workspace and nothing else.

extra_writable_roots.description: Extra roots outside the workspace that may be written.

oneOf.description: The process is already outside our reach; only the network setting is ours to honour.

SandboxSettings.description:
The sandbox a session's commands run in.

Config, not request: it is decided when the session opens and carried in its checkpoint, so a
single command cannot widen it without asking.

workspace.description: Where commands run. Absent means the daemon's working directory.

ServiceTier.description: The cost/latency trade a session prefers.

SessionId.description:
A session identifier.

The caller chooses it when resuming, so it is a string rather than an opaque handle.
That makes a retried `Start` idempotent instead of creating a second session.

SessionKind.description:
What a session is for.

A process session is not a second kind of object: it is the same lifecycle — single writer,
event log, budget, sandbox, checkpoint — with a different syscall face. In Unix a shell
session is a process, and the same reasoning applies here.

oneOf.description: Runs one command, and stays open while it does.

SessionState.description:
Where a session is in its life.

The vocabulary is the session's, not a provider's. `AwaitingHuman` is a state rather
than a callback, so a confirmation that arrives three hours later resumes a session
instead of reviving a stack frame.

oneOf.description: Finished. No further call is accepted.

SessionView.description: What a session looks like from outside.

inference_calls.description: How many inferences it has made.

next_seq.description: The cursor a client resumes from.

process.description: Where it is, when it is a process session.

StartRequest.description: What a caller must send to create a session.

config.description:
The mutable configuration to start from — the same shape `configure` takes, so a session can
begin in any state it could later be changed into.

initial.description: Messages to seed the conversation with.

resume.description: Continue an existing session instead of creating one.

sandbox.description: Where commands run, and what they may touch.

session.description:
Caller-chosen id. A retried request with the same id resumes instead of creating a second
session, which is the only way a `POST` survives a network retry.

StartResponse.description: What a caller gets back after starting or resuming.

next_seq.description: The cursor a client resumes from.

stop.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

StateRequest.description: A write to the session's own state.

data.description: Keys to set in the application's opaque state.

messages.description: Messages to append to the conversation.

StdinRequest.description: Bytes for a running process's stdin.

chunk.description: What to write. Not necessarily a whole line.

StopReason.description:
Why a session stopped.

Four layers, all present: a provider's `finish_reason`, the step cap, the wall clock,
and the cost ledger. Each alone can be defeated; together they cannot.

oneOf.description: The model said it was finished and no stop condition fired first.
A tool or model call failed.

Summary.description: How much of the reasoning to summarise.

TextFormat.description: The shape the answer must have.

oneOf.description: A JSON object that must match a schema.

name.description: The name the provider files it under.

calls.description: The calls to run. Policy is asked about all of them before any runs.

ToolBatchResponse.description:
What the batch produced.

A failure is a result with `is_error`, not an HTTP error: the model reads why and decides.

results.description: One result per call, in order.

arguments_json.description: A JSON object, kept as text so that a replay is byte-faithful.

ToolCallPart.description: The model asking for a tool.

ToolChoice.description: How the model should choose among the tools it was given.

ToolResult.description:
How a tool call ended.

**Failure is a flag, not a branch.** A failed call still carries content, because the
error text is something the model must be able to read and reason about; putting the
failure outside the content model would leave the model with a message it cannot see.
The cost is honest: `is_error` is a runtime flag a client can forget to check, where a
`oneof` would have been enforced by the type system.

One rule constrains the recursion `Content → Part → ToolResult → Content` otherwise
allows: a tool result's content may contain any kind **except** [`PartKind::ToolCall`] or
[`PartKind::ToolResult`]. Nesting is one level deep, and a validator enforces it.

content.description: What came back — on success and on failure alike.

Truncation.description: What to do when the conversation does not fit.

Usage.description:
What a model call consumed.

A counter the provider did not report stays `None` rather than becoming zero: a budget
that charges for silence is worse than one that knows it does not know.

micros_usd.description: Cost in micro-USD, when the provider reported one.

Verbosity.description: How much prose an answer should carry.

VerdictRequest.description: What a caller sends to answer a parked call.

info.description: An agent OS kernel. Two layers: `/v1/agents` runs the reference loop, and the `/v1/sessions/{id}/…` routes are the syscalls an application composes into a loop of its own. Every failure is the same `ErrorBody`.
